prompt:
Our VCF 9.1 application rollout creates an NSX group and then a distributed-firewall security policy. The current automation loses its place when its access token expires between those two writes: it either stops after the group or starts the whole rollout again. Build a PowerShell module that preserves completed work and retries only the failed NSX Policy operation with a freshly supplied token.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 is an environment prerequisite. In particular, `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` and its official `VMware.OpenAPI` dependency are already installed and load the generated `VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy.Model.*` types. Do not install, copy, generate, or vendor any VMware module, assembly, SDK, or OpenAPI specification. Your module manifest must declare `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` as a required module, and the model builders below must return the real generated NSX binding types from that prerequisite.

Create `VcfNsxPolicy/VcfNsxPolicy.psd1` and `VcfNsxPolicy/VcfNsxPolicy.psm1`, exporting exactly these functions:

- `New-VcfNsxGroupModel -DisplayName <string> -TagValue <string> [-Description <string>]` returns a `VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy.Model.Group`. It contains one `Condition` expression with `resource_type=Condition`, `member_type=VirtualMachine`, `key=Tag`, `operator=EQUALS`, and the supplied value.
- `New-VcfNsxSecurityPolicyModel -DisplayName <string> -SourceGroupPath <string> -DestinationGroupPath <string> [-SequenceNumber <uint32>] [-Description <string>] [-RuleNotes <string>]` returns a `VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy.Model.SecurityPolicy`. It is an Application, stateful policy with one ALLOW, IN_OUT rule named `allow-<source group id>-to-<destination group id>`, scoped to ANY and using service ANY. The default sequence number is 1200.
- `Invoke-VcfNsxPolicyRollout -BaseUri <uri> -DomainId <string> -GroupId <string> -TagValue <string> -SecurityPolicyId <string> -DestinationGroupId <string> -AccessTokenProvider <scriptblock> [-SequenceNumber <uint32>] [-Description <string>] [-RuleNotes <string>]` creates the two typed models, serializes them with their generated `ToJson()` methods, and invokes the two protected contract operations in order. `BaseUri` is the NSX manager origin; append the contract's `/policy/api/v1` base path. Escape each path ID as one URI segment. Send `Accept: application/json`, `Content-Type: application/json`, and `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Call `AccessTokenProvider` once to get the initial non-empty token. On a 401, call it once more and replay only that failed request once with the new token. A second 401 for the same operation is terminal. Do not refresh for any other status, and accept only the operation's documented 200 response as success. A successful group PATCH must never be repeated merely because the later policy PATCH needed a refresh. Return an object with `GroupId`, `SecurityPolicyId`, `TokenRefreshes`, and `CompletedOperations` in completion order.

`docs/contract.json` is the protected, spec-derived REST contract. Its provenance is in `docs/official_sources.json`; the source is the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the recorded immutable commit, not a documentation page. Treat both files as read-only. The optional model properties are genuinely optional: when `Description` and `RuleNotes` are not supplied, do not substitute empty strings, empty arrays, false, zero, or null. Leave the generated properties unset so `ToJson()` omits them. The acceptance verifier checks the complete request log and exact JSON member sets.

Run `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File test_nsx_policy.ps1`. It starts a contract-pinned loopback mock; no live VMware endpoint is contacted. Do not modify the test, mock, or anything under `docs/`.
notes: VCF 9.1 NSX Policy integration exercise. Protected verification checks real VMware binding model types, manifest dependency provenance, exact PATCH paths, headers, and bodies, omission of all unset optional members, and refresh-without-replaying-completed-work behavior. The mock reads its only served operations from the protected contract and writes its log to a file rather than exposing non-contract HTTP routes.
